newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends mostly lower on origin selling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends mostly lower on origin selling.

text.p: London robusta futures ended active dealings mostly lower on Monday with traders citing technical weakness and origin selling.
A total of 5,154 lots changed hands but what looked like a strong turnover was largely inflated by crosses, traders said.
"Technically it was overdone on the upside. There was a vacuum underneath," commented one.
Origin selling continued to cap any upside attempts but the market was underpinned by roaster buying at the lows, keeping prices in a narrow range.
Indonesia was the most actively selling origin, along with African producers such as Ivory Coast and Madagascar. Traders reckoned Vietnam was also not far off from hitting the market.

By the close, the benchmark November contract stood $2 higher at $1,522 after a session high of $1,534. The second-month January, which is mustering open interest to become the new benchmark, slipped $16 to $1,456 after a higher opening.
November gained ground in early trades but failed to maintain its rally above $1,530 a tonne.

One feature of the market was the widening Nov/Jan switch which saw trades from $48 to $64 amid significant trade house interest. Technical analysts said November was well supported by its shorter-term moving averages and recent trading lows around $1,511, followed by key support at $1,475.
